findings.title: The completed count against human limits
findings.claim: The focus's plural is counted exhaustively, and the wider comparison with 16:18 makes that completeness specific: humans cannot enumerate God's blessings, while the focus asserts a completed divine count of them. The plural can therefore be heard as fully accounted members, not merely a large number.
findings.mechanism: The carrier أَحْصَىٰهُمْ gives the exhaustive enumeration, and عَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا restates it as a completed count of the same plural. In 16:18, people are told that even counting God's favor cannot encompass it; this independent contrast sets human limitation beside the focus's completed divine act and changes the count from a bare total into a claim of comprehensive reach.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the difference between a large tally and a count that leaves no member outside it, with human inability to enumerate blessing supplying a wider measure of the focus's completeness.
findings.containment: 16:18 concerns blessings, not necessarily the focus's referent; the focus packet does not supply the antecedent of هم. This is a bounded cross-surah comparison, not a claim that the two verses count the same things, name a ledger, or specify the counted group's fate.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run finding is anchored to the two focus count branches. findings.title: From individual count to final accountability
findings.claim: The focus's exhaustive count can be heard within a wider accountability frame: one supplied connection promises a gathering of the counted plural, while others describe deeds counted despite being forgotten and no small or great deed left out of the record. This turns the focus's count from a bare total toward personal accountability, while the focus itself still names only its plural object.
findings.mechanism: أَحْصَىٰهُمْ carries the exhaustive count and عَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا makes the counting explicit. In 19:68 the supplied Arabic promises to gather and bring 'them'; in 58:6 God counts what people did although they forgot it; and 18:49 says the record leaves no small or great matter uncounted and that what people did is found present. Those distinct wider acts meet the focus's count and let it resonate as personal accountability rather than an abstract population total.
findings.reader_payoff: The count can be felt as protecting individual presence in the gathering and in the account of deeds, including what people themselves forgot; the image is more consequential than a headcount.
findings.containment: 19:94 itself mentions neither a Book, deeds, nor the gathering around Hell. The connections provide comparisons, not proof that every pronoun has the same antecedent or that the focus's object means deeds.
